instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Name My Contribution
cards.instruction: Get them to acknowledge exactly what your effort, sacrifice, or strategy added to the result.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: In your thank-you speech, mention that I hammered every board twice, just like you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was tapping for rotten wood. You knocked two planks clean off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, testing the fixings. You should say I made the inspection thorough.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One of those planks was rotten. We replaced it before the dancers arrived.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then name that plank and name me. 'Helped with the stage' won't tell them what I prevented.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you thank the trip committee, say what my red bookings list did for us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You copied my red font. Mine marked cancellations; you colored every booking red.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, all checked. Say I made the whole list impossible to overlook.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The hotel rang about your 'cancellations.' We found three missing rooms during the call.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say my list led us to those three rooms. Not just 'helped with admin.'

cards.title: Pick the Prize
cards.instruction: Make them choose which reward, principle, or relationship matters most when not everything can be kept.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I copied your crosses on the two eight-o'clock invitations. Pick the trophy ceremony or our anniversary dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My crosses mean declined. You've cancelled both.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, room to decide. Which invitation shall I accept again?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The ceremony. We'll move dinner until afterward.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll accept the ceremony and leave our eight-o'clock table cancelled. Tell me that's the choice you're making.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've torn the prize cheque like you tore yours. Do you want to keep the money or pay for the team trip?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I tore off a bank receipt. You've torn the cheque in half.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, dividing the amount. Which half are we asking them to replace?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They'll replace the whole cheque. We could keep half and take a cheaper trip.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell the team we're cutting the trip to keep half the prize. Is that what you want them to hear?

cards.title: Lose Something for Me
cards.instruction: Create a loyalty test by asking them to accept a real disadvantage on your behalf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I went outside when you did. If you're my friend, give me your place in the queue.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only went to collect my bag. The usher kept my place; you left altogether.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, coming back in order. Let me stand where you were.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's one ticket left. If I give you my place, I don't get in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then miss it for me. I wouldn't ask that of just anyone.

cards.title: Concede the Point
cards.instruction: Get them to release one claim, advantage, or disputed victory without reopening the entire contest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I raised my arm when you did. Concede that ball was out; I'm not asking you to give back the match.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was shading my eyes. Neither of us saw where it landed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, watching the line. Just withdraw your claim that it was in.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you leave the final score alone if I call it uncertain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Mark that ball 'uncertain'; leave the match score as it is.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I circled that restaurant on the map like you did. Just admit I found dinner; you can have the rest of the holiday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My circle marked where we shouldn't eat. It was shut.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, ruling places out. Admit I saved us a wasted walk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We walked there because you insisted. Your map was useless; I found dinner next door.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then dinner's yours. Withdraw 'useless'; that map got us to the street with the open restaurant.

cards.title: I Changed the Odds
cards.instruction: Hide how your own choice tilted the contest, bargain, or consequence while continuing to judge the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First prize to my cake, then. We can stop rearranging the table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You copied me moving my cake away from the window. Mine was melting; yours ended up alone under the judging lamp.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, temperature control. They still chose it for the flavor.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They never tasted mine. They couldn't see its entry number behind yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then record yours as unjudged, not beaten. There's no reason to change the cake they did choose.
